messages:
maria: quick idea — what if we add a single bot command that handles change windows, pinning, and a compact rollout/rollback flow? feels like we keep copying the same checklist into release notes.
chris: love it. do you mean one command to both schedule and control rollouts?
sam: +1. could help with oncall fatigue if it can do safe automatic rollbacks when certain signals spike.
maria: exactly. rough sketch: /release-orchestra with subcommands for start/promote/abort/rollback and meta flags for pin, canary %, change-window, and verification hooks.
olivia: can we make the verification hooks pluggable? e.g., smoke tests, latency monitors, and a quick quality eval.
maria: yes — pluggable checks. also want templates so product owners can define release-sets (model pin + infra config + post-check list) and apply with a single flag.
chris: sketching a CLI usage:
```bash
/release-orchestra start --env=prod --window=60m --pin=model:redwood-v2.1 --canary=10
/release-orchestra promote --to=100 --verify=smoke,latency:95th<200ms
/release-orchestra rollback --reason="latency spike" --revert-pin
```
sam: nice. make sure promote can accept a fallback variant, e.g. --fallback=model:redwood-v2.0-quant so we can keep serving if main fails.
maria: yep, auto-fallback policy should be first-class: thresholds -> fallback -> alert oncall. also want a short templating syntax for release notes, something like template:performance-beta -> expands to pins + checklist + postmortem link.
olivia: ops question: who can run this in prod? RBAC needed. maybe require two approvals for certain flags (revert-pin, bypass-verifications).
maria: good point — add `--require-approvals=2` or tie to a policy. by default, engineers can start in staging; prod requires approval.
deploy-bot: scheduled release request received: id=ro-1911004327-1. status=queued waiting for approvals.
chris: can the bot auto-generate a release summary block for docs and the release channel? small markdown blob we can paste into release notes.
maria: yes, auto summary + link to template + artifacts. also store the rollout steps as an auditable trace.
sam: automation idea: add a `--dry-run` that outputs the exact commands that would run (pins, route changes, cache flushes) so SRE can validate quickly.
maria: agreed. last thought — we should keep the core commands tiny and let templates drive the complexity. templates live in a repo, referenced by name. developers can add template PRs rather than editing the bot.
olivia: sounds good. next steps? prototype slash command + small state machine in a lambda, then wire to deploy-bot for execution. I can take the approvals/RBAC piece.
maria: I'll (a) draft the command spec and example templates, (b) mock the bot responses, (c) open a RFC. Sam/chris/olivia — want quick review tomorrow?
sam: yes
chris: count me in
olivia: on it
deploy-bot: reminder — keeper policy: if latency 95th >200ms for 3m AND error-rate >1% then auto-rollback to fallback. logging will include rollout id.
maria: perfect — I'll include that policy in the RFC and add sample config. thanks team :rocket:
